Level 1 charging uses the same 120 volt current found in standard household
outlets and can be performed using the EVSE that comes with an EV from the
automaker. This typically provides about 5 miles of range per hour of
charging. Offering level 1 charging can be as simple as installing dedicated
120 volt outlets in a parking area, as VTrans has done at a number of
recently constructed park and ride facilities.

Level 2 charging uses 240 volt power to enable faster regeneration of an EV
battery system – usually about 10-20 miles of range per hour of charging
depending on the vehicle and EVSE power capability. Providing this type of
charging requires installation of a dedicated EVSE charging device and
electrical wiring capable of handling higher voltage power.

DCFC provides compatible vehicles (generally all-electric models) with an
80% charge in 20-30 minutes by converting high voltage AC power to DC
power outside of the vehicle for storage in EV batteries. This provides 100+
miles of range per hour of charging. Currently most DCFC compatible
vehicles can handle up to 50 kW of DCFC power, but higher powered, faster
charging DCFC is expected to be widely available in vehicles arriving over the
next few years with charging power up to 300 kW or more.
